title: KTP Deployment Profile — Unreleased v3
description: The unreleased v3 declaration surface for a KTP deployment (specifications/deployment-profile.md). This version replaces inactivity-based standing decay with a required binding to a scoped readiness profile while preserving historical resilience. The published v2 schema is archived separately as deployment-profile-legacy-v2.json. This schema constrains shape; identifier-level validity (signal IDs exist, alias-set membership, synthetic-signal normalization coverage) is validated against catalog/ by scripts/check-declarations.py — the catalogue stays the single source of those lists. The checker also enforces weight and threshold finiteness, the six Risk Factor weights' unit sum, envelope-threshold ordering, standing-policy binding shape, and Oracle membership uniqueness and quorum bounds; schema validation alone is insufficient for those semantic checks or current authorization.

profile_id.description: Stable identifier for this deployment profile. Records reference the profile as <profile_id>@<version> — the normalization-profile identifier carried by [KTP-AUDIT] 3.2 sensor_health (per #72).

version.description: Monotonic profile version. Any change to any declaration increments it; a value computed under one profile version must not be replayed against another.

risk_factors.description: The D2 bridge: each Risk Factor is a named aggregation over a declared subset of Context Signals. The required array is the #83 arity: six weighted inputs. Their finite, positive weights must sum to 1; check-declarations.py checks the sum exactly over the decimal representations of parsed numbers, without tolerance or rescaling. The Soul veto is not a term and is declared in soul_veto.

soul_veto.description: The sovereignty frameworks queried before aggregation ([KTP-SENSORS] 4.3). Evaluated before R; any veto or any UNDETERMINED query reads S = 1 (per #83, #105).

frameworks.description: Identifiers of the sovereignty registries/frameworks queried.

feeds.description: The wire-to-catalogue mapping (#106): which catalogue signals each configured feed populates. Keys are feed ids as configured in [KTP-SENSORS] 2.2 / sensor-config.json. Stays in configuration; does not ride the wire.

aliases.description: For each alias set (catalog/index.json alias_sets) of which this deployment populates any member: the member it populates. Keys are set names; values are the populated signal ID, which check-declarations.py validates as a member of the named set.

normalization.description: Per aggregated synthetic bare-0-1 signal (zero_one: 'synthetic' in catalog/*.json): the normalization function. Ratio rows declare a population on the catalogue row instead; determined rows declare neither.

method.description: Named normalization method (e.g. min-max over a declared source range, z-score to logistic, vendor-documented mapping).

parameters.description: The method's parameters, sufficient for a relying party to reproduce the mapping.

label_sets.description: Per aggregated categorical signal, and per denominator predicate (declared under the signal whose denominator it gates): the label set populated (#68). Derived signals inherit the label set's cardinality.

source.description: Citation or registry identifier for the taxonomy, where one exists.

predicate.description: Where this entry declares a denominator predicate rather than the signal's own value categories: the predicate word (e.g. 'healthy').

peer_share.description: The peer-signal share of E_base, in points (ktp-core 5.1). Zero where peer validation is not implemented; otherwise within 5.5.5's 10-20. Echoed in the Trust Proof; no cross-deployment magnitude comparison across differing shares.

hop_bound.description: Maximum accountability-chain length accepted; the normative ceiling is 12 (ktp-core 5.1). An attestation whose chain exceeds it computes as zero.

adjudicator.description: The declared adjudicator for findings of misattestation, including for-cause withdrawal claims. MUST be neither the attestor nor the subject agent.

standing_policy.description: Required exact binding to an independently approved readiness profile. Historical resilience is retained; current authority additionally requires fresh verified readiness for the requested operation and exact subject/scope. This declaration alone neither approves the profile nor grants authority. Changes use the protected profile-change process described in specifications/operational-readiness.md. The digest binds the RFC 8785 canonical readiness-profile payload; Level 3 requires SHA-384 as selected by the trusted cryptographic profile. The legacy standing_decay_rate field is invalid in v3.

version.description: Positive safe integer token. The declaration checker rejects booleans and parsed floats, including integral floats.

human_policy.description: Required before accepting human actions or human-origin delegation. Omission disables human eligibility and MUST NOT enable legacy human scoring. Binds the complete JCS human profile and a durable version floor; declaration shape is not governance approval or authority. See specifications/human-eligibility.md.

version.description: Positive safe integer token. The declaration checker rejects booleans and parsed floats, including integral floats.

emergency_policy.description: Optional binding to a separately approved emergency policy. Omission disables this capability; a reference alone does not prove approval or activate it. Policy changes and changes to this binding require specifications/emergency-capability.md's protected process. The digest covers the exact UTF-8 policy payload bytes.

digest.description: Level 3 deployments require SHA-384. The trusted deployment's cryptographic profile determines the algorithm requirement; declaration shape alone cannot establish it.

oracle_consensus.description: Optional declaration for a Byzantine Oracle mesh. Omission makes no Byzantine mesh claim. The checker requires distinct declared node, key, and control-domain identities and N >= 3f + 1, floor((N + f) / 2) + 1 <= quorum <= N - f. Shape and arithmetic do not prove signature validity, actual independence, protocol review, or correct runtime consensus. The complete protocol specification is pinned by exact payload digest.

protocol_spec_digest.description: Digest of the exact protocol-specification bytes. The trusted deployment's cryptographic profile determines the required algorithm; Level 3 requires SHA-384. This field does not attest review of those bytes.

membership_epoch.description: Authenticated membership epoch; positive integer tokens only. The checker rejects booleans and parsed floats, including integral floats. Declaration validity does not authorize an epoch change.

members.description: Exact member roster. Each node_id, key_id, and control_domain must be independently unique across the roster, enforced by check-declarations.py. Distinct labels do not prove real administrative or key-custody independence.

fault_tolerance.description: Declared maximum Byzantine members f. The checker rejects booleans and parsed floats; requires N >= 3f + 1.

quorum.description: Minimum distinct eligible voting members for protected decisions, not a count of messages or merely signature shares. The checker rejects booleans and parsed floats and enforces floor((N + f) / 2) + 1 <= quorum <= N - f. A protocol may impose stricter constraints.

envelope_thresholds.description: Supervision thresholds for the decision contract (ktp-core 6.6). Declared thresholds must be finite numbers satisfying 0 <= m_veto < m_allow. The cross-field ordering and finite-number checks are enforced by check-declarations.py. Omission retains the existing m_veto = m_allow = 0 default, including its equality veto; an explicitly declared equal pair is invalid. Profile thresholds never relax the independent A > E or zero-capacity veto.

oracle_literal.description: Exact nonempty identifier without whitespace or wildcard characters.

signal_id.description: A Context Signal ID, domain.group.name, resolved against catalog/*.json.

signals.description: The declared subset of Context Signals feeding this factor. MUST NOT include more than one ID from an alias set.

method.description: The named aggregation (e.g. weighted_average, max, min).

parameters.description: The method's parameters (e.g. per-signal weights), sufficient for a relying party to reproduce the aggregation.

weight.description: The factor's finite weight w_i in R = sum(w_i * s_i), strictly greater than 0 and at most 1. The six factor weights must sum to 1, checked by scripts/check-declarations.py; an invalid declaration is rejected, never silently rescaled. This does not constrain per-feed aggregation weights.
